chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches FireIncident → OilRefinery; minting a new property.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: archivedAt
candidates.comment: An archived at relation between a creative work and the URL or web page where an archived version of it can be found. Also called archival location, preserved at, stored at. Examples: "A news article's archived at is 'archive.org/news-article-url'.", "The web page's archived at is 'web.archive.org/page-snapshot'."

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

chosen_property.label: distanceFromUkrainianBorder
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the distance of an oil refinery from the Ukrainian border.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property links OilRefinery to Distance; a new property is created.

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: mileageFromOdometer
candidates.comment: An odometer mileage relation between a vehicle and the total distance traveled as read from its odometer. Also called: odometer reading, total mileage, distance traveled. Examples: "Car mileageFromOdometer '50000 KMT'", "Truck mileageFromOdometer '120000 SMI'", "Motorcycle mileageFromOdometer '15000 km'".

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: geoRadius
candidates.comment: A geo radius relation between a geo circle and its approximate radial distance from the center. Also called: circle radius, geographic radius, extent. Examples: "Search Area GeoCircle" geo radius "5000 meters", "Weather Alert Zone" geo radius "10 miles", "GPS Accuracy Circle" geo radius "10 feet".

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: marginOfError
candidates.comment: A margin of error relation between an observation and its quantitative value representing the error range. Also called: error margin, uncertainty range, confidence interval. Examples: "Poll Result marginOfError '±3%'", "Scientific Measurement marginOfError '0.5 units'", "Survey Data marginOfError '2 percentage points'".

candidates.label: busNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a bus trip and its unique identifier. Also called "bus ID", "bus route number", "bus identifier". Examples: "Bus trip from NYC to Boston busNumber 'B101'", "Local route 10 bus trip busNumber '4567'". Distinct from busName, which is a human-readable name, whereas busNumber is a unique identifier.

candidates.label: availableAtOrFrom
candidates.comment: A place from which an offer can be obtained. Also called: pickup location, sales point, distribution point. Examples: "Offer 'Groceries' availableAtOrFrom 'Supermarket A'", "Offer 'Concert Tickets' availableAtOrFrom 'Venue Box Office'."

candidates.label: departureBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port from which it departs. Also called: origin boat terminal, departure port, ferry terminal. Examples: "Ferry Trip" departure boat terminal "Dover Ferry Terminal", "Cruise" departure boat terminal "PortMiami". Distinct from arrivalBoatTerminal, which is the destination terminal.

chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property; minting a new one.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: associatedDisease

Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. candidates.label: relatedCondition

Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."
